guard_streams.source: Ofcom open data and official data notes

facts.detail: Ofcom provides applicable Connected Nations downloads on an open basis under the Open Government Licence, subject to its conditions.
Open licensing governs permitted reuse and does not replace source, schema, archive or join validation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Licence status cannot raise candidate confidence.

guard_streams.source: Official fixed-performance and mobile data notes

facts.detail: The official data notes specify comma-separated files with double-quote text delimiters where applicable.
Ofcom supplies a Connected Nations data-team route for questions and feedback on the published data.

guard_streams.write_limit: Documented format and contact metadata are not exact archive-byte evidence.

facts.detail: Connected Nations is currently published twice a year.
The main report is typically released toward year end and an interim update in spring.

guard_streams.write_limit: Publication cadence cannot be used to interpolate missing postcode values.

facts.detail: The accompanying interactive report includes latest and historical data.
Ofcom describes the downloadable files as some of the data underpinning the report rather than a universal parcel-level database.

guard_streams.write_limit: Historical or interactive aggregates cannot replace the exact all-premises r2 postcode member.

guard_streams.source: About this data – fixed broadband performance 2025

facts.detail: The 2025 fixed-performance collection received active-line information from 57 fixed broadband providers.
The performance data is a July 2025 snapshot of active residential and business broadband connections.

guard_streams.write_limit: Active-line performance is temporally and semantically separate from January 2026 coverage availability.

guard_streams.source: About this data – fixed broadband performance 2025

facts.detail: From 2024 the performance analysis uses maximum speeds, whereas earlier reports used average speeds and different speed ranges.
Monthly data usage is now derived from aggregated volumes at the OLT or headend rather than per-line measurements.

guard_streams.write_limit: Pre-2024 series and per-line interpretations are not directly comparable with the current method.

guard_streams.source: About this data – fixed broadband performance 2025

facts.detail: Current fixed-performance files cover local authorities, Westminster constituencies, devolved constituencies and census output areas.
Since 2024 Ofcom no longer reports fixed-performance speeds at postcode level.

guard_streams.write_limit: No performance value may be downscaled from these geographies to a postcode or parcel.

guard_streams.source: About this data – fixed broadband performance 2025

facts.detail: The July 2025 census-output-area performance file documents 238,864 rows.
An output area is included only when speed information exists for at least five lines.

guard_streams.write_limit: The five-line disclosure threshold does not establish parcel identity or universal OA coverage.

guard_streams.source: About this data – fixed broadband performance 2025

facts.detail: Average maximum-speed fields are grouped into below 10, 10–30, 30–100, 100–300 and 300–900 Mbit/s download bands.
Connections with maximum download speed of at least 900 Mbit/s have a separate field.

guard_streams.write_limit: Performance-band averages are not maximum-available coverage percentages.

guard_streams.source: About this data – fixed broadband performance 2025

facts.detail: Ofcom applies one-decimal or nearest-integer rounding depending on the download or upload speed band.
Average monthly usage fields are local-authority-only and combine download plus upload for all technologies or full fibre.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded aggregate speeds and usage cannot be written as parcel measurements.

guard_streams.source: About this data – mobile coverage Spring 2026

facts.detail: Mobile 5G and 5G SA coverage uses High Confidence and Very High Confidence prediction categories.
The mobile data note provides 5G and 5G SA coverage only for outdoor premises and geographic coverage, separate from fixed broadband speed data.

guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile signal predictions cannot populate fixed broadband postcode metrics.

facts.detail: The planned-deployment report describes operator plans extending from January 2026 to January 2029.
Ofcom reports around 6,950 additional geographically distinct FWA masts planned or set for upgrade across the UK.

guard_streams.write_limit: Planned deployment is prospective and cannot be treated as current January 2026 coverage.
